global_decisions: Severity follows the draft's strength table: MUST -> flag (blocks publish until fixed or waived with a reason); SHOULD -> warning (needs a reason, doesn't block); GUIDE -> review lens (never flagged). Deterministic MUST checks with near-zero false positives are 'error'.
Precedence: PRIN rules win conflicts (as the draft says); a specific rule is cited over an umbrella rule; a reviewer's context reason (CONS-02) clears consistency warnings.
Review unit is the Sabad: 'first use' and 'same word' are scoped to one Sabad.
Every rule runs only on the layers it applies to (literal, transcreation, publication).
Wording (PRIN-04): flags say 'differs from reference rendering'. 'Approved' is used only as a workflow status, never as 'correct'.
'Same word' grouping uses the stem key from BaniDB text; the ending matra is kept as a feature for grammar hints.
Open SikhRI questions never become flags: Eko reports variation within a Sabad, not a choice it can't verify.
Scope: Eko reviews the English transcreation only, and never generates translation text.
No roles: anyone may resolve a finding, propose a rule, or approve one, always with a written reason.

rules.text: Interpret according to Gurmat, the principles of the Guru's Wisdom.
ambiguities: 'Gurmat' is not operationalized; no observable test in English text.

rules.text: Treat internal evidence from the Guru Granth Sahib itself as the primary authority. Outside resources are consulted but rank below it.
ambiguities: Governs research sources, not the output text; nothing for Eko to read.

rules.text: Present every rendering as the team's current understanding, not a final one. Understanding is expected to change as the relationship with Sabad deepens.

prefilter.notes: Publication-level presence check for the humility note (see 'Standard disclaimer' under section 1). Eko's demo input is per-line text, so this needs Sabad-level publication data.

ambiguities: Is there a canonical wording for the humility note, or only the three ideas (Sabad infinite, understanding finite, reading may evolve)?
Does the note attach per Sabad, per Bani, or per publication?

resolution.decision: Removed from automated checks by the team (Oct 16). Reviewer asked to confirm (Q1).

rules.text: Never label a rendering as the single correct translation, or other translations as wrong. Multiple renderings can coexist.

prefilter.notes: High precision, low recall. 'true'/'real' + 'meaning' also occurs in ordinary content ('the true friend'), so those hits go to LLM confirmation. Most real occurrences will be in commentary/footnotes, which Eko does not ingest.

ambiguities: Applies to claims about translations; also constrains Eko's own UI wording (avoid 'approved/correct' vs 'wrong').
Unclear whether a footnote saying another rendering 'misses' a nuance counts as labelling it wrong.

resolution.decision: Prefilter + LLM confirm on claims of a single correct reading or that other renderings are wrong. Eko's own UI follows this rule too: flags say 'differs from reference rendering', never 'incorrect'.

rules.text: Keep transcreation distinct from translation. They are separate deliverables with separate rules (see LAYER).
ambiguities: Principle only; the checkable forms are LAYER-07 (no parentheses) and LAYER-08 (no mirroring). Eko should cite those, not PRIN-05.

rules.text: Aim for closeness and intimacy, so the reader can engage personally with the Guru's teachings.
ambiguities: GUIDE level: 'closeness and intimacy' has no testable definition yet.

rules.text: Connect contemporary readers to Sabad within their present social, cultural and linguistic context.
ambiguities: GUIDE level; overlaps LAYER-06 (contemporary English).

rules.text: Assume a global reader with no prior knowledge; supply context and clarification accordingly.
ambiguities: 'Supply context' is unbounded; the checkable slice is 'transcribed term glossed on first use' (TERM-03/07).
Where should context go: in-line in the transcreation, or in footnotes (CONS-04)?

rules.text: Draw on, and openly acknowledge, diverse schools of thought; name where interpretations diverge rather than hiding it.
ambiguities: Applies to commentary, which Eko does not ingest. Duplicates FLOW-07.

resolution.decision: Duplicate of FLOW-07; out of scope for text checks.

rules.text: Do not render the Divine as "God" or "Lord". These terms project connotations onto the Guru-Wisdom that the original does not carry.

prefilter.notes: Tier 1 is case-sensitive (capitalized forms = Divine reference): flag directly. Tier 2 (lowercase/plural/goddess) goes to LLM to decide whether the referent is the Divine. Word boundaries exclude 'landlord', 'warlord'.

ambiguities: Rule says 'render the Divine as'; the reviewer checklist says 'No God or Lord anywhere'. Is a worldly lord/master, another tradition's 'God', or a quoted title (e.g. a deity epithet) also banned?
Lowercase and plural forms (gods, lords, goddess) for deities or rulers: in scope or not?
Quoted text inside notes (e.g. citing another translator's 'God') would false-positive if notes are ever ingested.

resolution.decision: The rule text governs: it bans 'God'/'Lord' as renderings of the Divine. The checklist's 'anywhere' is read as shorthand. Capitalized God/Lord (and Godhead, Lordship, Lord-X) -> error, deterministic L1. Lowercase or plural (gods, lords, goddess) -> LLM confirms the referent with the BaniDB line; a worldly or other-tradition referent passes.

rules.text: Retain the specific Divine attribute the original Sabad uses (for example, a name meaning Creator stays Creator) rather than collapsing every name into one English word.

prefilter.notes: Gurmukhi-side prefilter on the BaniDB line (stems from the Section 8 'Divine names' list; inflected endings need normalization). If a name is found, LLM checks whether the English keeps that name's specific attribute or collapses it into a generic word.

right: a name meaning Creator stays Creator

ambiguities: No name-to-attribute table exists yet (Section 8 gap 'Divine names'); without it the LLM's own sense of each name's meaning is the reference, so FP risk is high.
When is a name kept untranslated instead of rendered by attribute (Section 8)?
Is 'the Divine' an acceptable rendering for any name, or always a collapse?

resolution.decision: Narrowed until SikhRI supplies the Divine-name table (Section 8 gap). Two checks only: (a) names whose attribute is explicit in the word itself: the karta/kartar family must keep 'Creator' (the rule's own example) -> flag. (b) collapse detector: 3+ distinct Divine names in one Sabad all rendered by the same single English word -> warning for the reviewer. Eko does not judge other names' renderings yet.

rules.text: Use "IkOankar" for the core Divine concept, glossed on first use as One Universal Integrative Force (1Force, the One).

prefilter.notes: Spelling check: any variant (Ik Onkar, Ek Onkar, Ik Oankar, Ekankar, Ik Omkar ...) that is not exactly 'IkOankar' is flagged. Gloss check: within the first-use scope, the first 'IkOankar' should be accompanied by 'One Universal Integrative Force'. The ੴ symbol on the Gurmukhi line can serve as a trigger.

right: One Universal Integrative Force (1Force, the One)

ambiguities: 'First use' scope: per Sabad, per Bani, per page, or per publication?
Gloss format conflicts with layer rules: parentheses mean 'added words' in the literal (LAYER-03) and are banned in the transcreation (LAYER-07).
Are '1Force' and 'the One' alternative glosses, or required alongside 'One Universal Integrative Force'?

resolution.decision: Exact spelling 'IkOankar'; any variant -> warning. First use = first occurrence in the Sabad. Gloss 'One Universal Integrative Force' at first use, written as an apposition (comma or dash), because LAYER-07 bans parentheses in the transcreation.

rules.text: Avoid English terms with Judeo-Christian undertones when describing Sikh concepts. The named example: do not call the Guru Granth Sahib "scripture" or "canon".

prefilter.notes: Named terms only. Co-occurrence with a GGS/Sikh referent = flag; bare hits go to LLM to check the referent (e.g. 'scriptures' used for other traditions' books named on the source line). The rule's general clause ('Judeo-Christian undertones') is not encoded; see Section 8 'Loaded words'.

ambiguities: General clause is open-ended; only 'scripture'/'canon' are named. Soul, sin, heaven, salvation, worship, prayer, saint, hymn are listed as an open gap (Section 8), not banned.
Is 'scripture' acceptable when rendering a source word that refers to non-Sikh books?

resolution.decision: Removed from automated checks by the team (Oct 16). Reviewer asked to confirm (Q1).

rules.text: Equally avoid Hindu or Indological terms that misframe Sikh concepts. The named example: do not call the Guru Granth Sahib "ved" or "shastra".

prefilter.notes: Same structure as TERM-04. Bare hits are common and legitimate because Gurbani itself refers to the Vedas and Shastras; if the Gurmukhi line contains those words, a bare hit is almost certainly a faithful rendering, not a breach.

ambiguities: General clause ('Hindu or Indological terms that misframe') is open-ended beyond the two named examples.
Lower precision than TERM-04 because legitimate references to the Vedas/Shastras are frequent in the source.

resolution.decision: Removed from automated checks by the team (Oct 16). Reviewer asked to confirm (Q1).

rules.text: Before choosing an English equivalent for any term, check what the English word's own history implies; near-equivalents are not neutral.
ambiguities: Describes a translator's research step; Eko can at most surface loaded words for a reviewer.

resolution.decision: Review lens only.

rules.text: Keep core Sikh terms in transcribed form, with a gloss, where English has no faithful equivalent. Terms SikhRI uses this way include Sabad (Infinite Wisdom), Nam (Identification with IkOankar), Bani, Gurmat, Panth (Collective), Patshah (Sovereign) and Prakash Purab (Illumination Day).

prefilter.notes: Patterns are applied per span; when several tiers hit the same span, the most specific action wins. Two checks: (1) non-preferred spellings of the listed terms (deterministic); (2) English substitutes such as 'the Word', 'the Name', 'hymn' (LLM confirm; lowercase 'word'/'name' are ordinary English). Proper nouns such as Bani titles may legitimately use common spellings (TRAN-02).

ambiguities: Bani and Gurmat are listed without a gloss although the rule requires one.
Gloss format per layer is undefined (parentheses conflict with LAYER-03/LAYER-07).
Listed forms carry no diacritics (Nam, not Nām); unclear whether TRAN rules apply to Sikh terms in English running text.
List is 'terms SikhRI uses this way include' = non-exhaustive; full list should come from the SikhRI glossary.

resolution.decision: Non-preferred spellings (Shabad, Naam, Padshah, Parkash Purab) -> warning; titles of Banis are proper nouns and exempt. English substitutes ('the Word', 'the Name', 'hymn') -> LLM confirm -> warning. Missing gloss at first use in the Sabad -> hint only.

rules.text: When the same word repeats in a Sabad, render it with the same English word throughout that Sabad.
ambiguities: 'Same word': same surface form, or same lemma across inflected endings (matra changes case/number)?
Does it apply to the literal only, or also to the transcreation (which LAYER-08 frees from the source)?
SHOULD-level and from Sabad notes; CONS-02 (MUST) requires departure when context changes meaning. Eko should report 'inconsistent, needs reason', not 'error'.
Draft says TERM-08 states 'the same principle as TERM-02 at line level'; they differ (TERM-02 = attribute fidelity, TERM-08 = repetition consistency).

resolution.decision: Inactive: applies to the literal translation, which is out of scope (transcreation only). Earlier call kept for later: Literal layer only (LAYER-08 frees the transcreation). 'Same word' = same stem key from the morphology analyzer within one Sabad, so inflected forms group together. Differing renderings -> warning, cleared by a reviewer reason (CONS-02/03).

rules.text: Check the project glossary and prior renderings before introducing a new English equivalent (see CONS).

prefilter.notes: Populate from SikhRI glossary and the published sample renderings when they arrive; flag an English equivalent for a term that differs from every prior rendering of that term.

ambiguities: Process step; Eko can only check the outcome (new equivalent vs prior ones), which needs the project glossary/sample. Largely duplicates CONS-01.

resolution.decision: Merged into CONS-01 (same check).

rules.text: Do not write a transcreation for a line until its words have been annotated and its literal translation exists.
ambiguities: Ordering ('until') is not visible in final text; only presence (annotation + literal exist when a transcreation exists) is checkable, and only once annotation data is available.

resolution.decision: Process rule. Eko has no annotation data, so this stays p1.

rules.text: Organize work by Bani (composition) rather than linearly through the volume.
ambiguities: Workflow organization; not observable in text.

rules.text: For every term, weigh layer 1, words and terms: each word carries multiple meanings, connotations and history that cannot fully cross into English.
ambiguities: Deliberation duty; no observable artifact.

rules.text: Weigh layer 2, historical implications: near-equivalent English terms carry their own developed connotations (see TERM-04 to 06).
ambiguities: Deliberation duty; its observable outcome is covered by TERM-04 to 06.

rules.text: Weigh layer 3, the audience: decide how much prior knowledge to assume, and how much added context the English needs to be intelligible.
ambiguities: Deliberation duty; overlaps PRIN-08 and CONS-04.

rules.text: Decide, per passage, where to sit between strict literal faithfulness and smooth, meaningful English. Record the choice.
ambiguities: 'Record the choice' implies a log; where it is recorded is unspecified. Could become p1 if a decision log is shared.

rules.text: Ground the commentary in a range of interpretive schools and discuss where they diverge.
ambiguities: Commentary layer; duplicates PRIN-09.

rules.text: Retain every word, meaning, grammatical position and context present in the source line.
ambiguities: Four things in one rule: word, meaning, grammatical position, context. Word omission is checkable with medium confidence; grammatical position (case, number, person from endings) is low without SikhRI annotation data.
'Every meaning' of a polysemous word: all senses in the literal, or the one in context?
How are implicit or compound words counted?

resolution.decision: Inactive: applies to the literal translation, which is out of scope (transcreation only). Earlier call kept for later: Possible omissions only: the LLM lists content words in the BaniDB line with no English counterpart. Non-blocking hint, because without annotation data Eko can't verify grammatical position. 'Grammatical position' is read as grammatical role, not word order (see LAYER-04).

rules.text: Set the literal translation in italics.

prefilter.notes: Deterministic markup check on rich text; no LLM step needed. Plain-text input (current demo) carries no italics, hence p1.

ambiguities: What represents italics in plain-text or API exports?
Does italics extend to parenthesized additions inside the literal?
The layer table also says the transcreation is Roman (upright); that has no rule ID.

resolution.decision: Inactive: applies to the literal translation, which is out of scope (transcreation only). Earlier call kept for later: Satisfied by design: Eko stores each layer separately and always renders the literal in italics, so italics can't be wrong. The transcreation is rendered upright (the draft's layer table).

rules.text: Put any English word added for readability, clarity or poetic balance inside parentheses, so it is visibly not in the source.
ambiguities: Do English function words required by grammar (articles, copulas, prepositions that express a case ending) count as 'added'? If yes, nearly every line is full of parentheses; if no, the boundary needs examples.
Prepositions derived from Gurmukhi case endings (matra) are not additions, so a naive alignment check will false-positive.
Only the format half (balanced, non-empty, non-nested parentheses) is deterministic; finding unmarked additions needs source alignment.
Glosses (TERM-03/07) written in parentheses would be indistinguishable from added words.

resolution.decision: Inactive: applies to the literal translation, which is out of scope (transcreation only). Earlier call kept for later: Two parts. (1) Parentheses must be balanced, non-empty and not nested -> error, deterministic. (2) Unmarked additions: the LLM flags added content words (nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs) with no source counterpart -> hint. Grammar-required function words (articles, copulas, case prepositions) are not flagged until annotation data exists. Parentheses holding a known gloss (TERM-03/07) are exempt.

rules.text: Sentence order may be rearranged when needed for comprehension; meaning may not be added outside parentheses.
ambiguities: First clause is a permission: Eko must not flag word-order changes in the literal.
Second clause restates LAYER-03; suggest Eko cites LAYER-03 for unmarked additions and uses LAYER-04 as a suppressor.

resolution.decision: Inactive: applies to the literal translation, which is out of scope (transcreation only). Earlier call kept for later: Suppressor: word-order changes are never flagged. Meaning added outside parentheses is reported under LAYER-03.

rules.text: Where possible, preserve the poetic balance and beauty of the line despite English lacking the source languages' oral roots.
ambiguities: GUIDE level; 'poetic balance and beauty' undefined.

resolution.decision: Review lens only.

rules.text: Write in contemporary English; the aim is resonance with today's reader.

prefilter.notes: Archaism list is high precision; ambiguous short words ('art', 'ye', 'lo') and -eth/-est endings ('best', 'rest', 'forest') need LLM confirmation.

ambiguities: Section 8 lists 'Register: are archaisms (thee, thou) banned?' as open, although this MUST rule seems to answer it. Confirm with SikhRI.
Beyond archaisms, 'contemporary English' is judgment (diction, idiom).
Applies to the transcreation only; archaisms in the literal are not covered by any rule.

resolution.decision: Closed archaism list (thee, thou, thy, hath, unto ...) -> flag. Ambiguous words (art, ye, lo) and -eth/-est endings -> LLM confirm. Treats LAYER-06 as settling the archaism part of the Section 8 'Register' question; plain vs elevated register stays open.

rules.text: Do not use parentheses; the transcreation is not a translation and nothing in it is marked as added.

prefilter.notes: Deterministic; any parenthesis in a transcreation is a breach. LLM step not needed except for square brackets.

ambiguities: Square brackets: also banned?
Conflicts with glossing in parentheses (TERM-03/07): how is a gloss written in the transcreation?

resolution.decision: Any parenthesis or square bracket in a transcreation -> error, deterministic. Brackets count, because they also mark text as added.

rules.text: Do not force the transcreation to mirror the original line, the literal translation or the Panjabi transcreation.
ambiguities: 'Do not force ... to mirror' has no threshold. Proposed signal: token overlap or edit similarity between transcreation and literal above a cutoff calibrated on the SikhRI sample, then LLM/reviewer.
Mirroring the Panjabi transcreation is uncheckable (no data).
Short lines may legitimately be close to the literal; tension with LAYER-09 'building on the literal'.

resolution.decision: Inactive: comparing against the literal needs a literal translation, which is out of scope. Revisit if SikhRI's sample includes literals as context.

rules.text: Use the transcreation to elaborate, contextualize and expound the line, building on the literal translation.
ambiguities: How much elaboration is expected (Section 8 'Length' gap)?
A derived check ('transcreation contradicts the literal') is useful but not stated in the rule.

resolution.decision: Review lens only; LAYER-08's check covers the measurable half.

rules.text: Capture the essence of the attributes of IkOankar as they appear in the original (TERM-01 to 03 apply here with full force).
ambiguities: Umbrella rule: Eko should cite TERM-01 to 03 when flagging the transcreation, and use LAYER-10 only as a reviewer lens to avoid double flags.

resolution.decision: Umbrella over TERM-01 to 03. Never raises its own flag; Eko cites the specific TERM rule.

rules.text: Default to the English rendering already used for the same or a similar term elsewhere in the project.

prefilter.notes: Term-to-rendering map built from SikhRI's published sample; flag a rendering that differs from the established one for the same lemma.

ambiguities: 'Same or a similar term': similarity is undefined.
Needs project-wide renderings, which arrive later as a SikhRI sample.

resolution.decision: Active once the SikhRI sample arrives: a stem whose reference rendering differs from the draft -> warning 'differs from reference rendering, add a reason'. Absorbs TERM-09.

rules.text: Depart from the default when context requires it. Rigid consistency that ignores context is a misrepresentation.
ambiguities: Exemption rule: it changes how Eko reports inconsistency (a question for the reviewer, not an error). Not itself a flag.

resolution.decision: Precedence rule: a reviewer's context reason clears any consistency warning (TERM-08, CONS-01). It never raises a flag itself.

rules.text: Never vary a rendering without a reason. Each departure from the default needs a recorded justification.

prefilter.notes: Reuse CONS-01 departure detection, then look for a matching footnote or term-log entry.

ambiguities: Where justifications are recorded (footnote vs term log) and in what format; Eko needs read access to it.

resolution.decision: Satisfied by workflow: Eko won't let a consistency warning be waived without a written reason, and stores that reason as the log.

rules.text: Decide, per case, whether an explanatory footnote is needed, weighing the audience's expectations.
ambiguities: Per-case judgment; footnotes are not ingested.

resolution.decision: Review lens only.

rules.text: List all literal meanings and the implied meaning of the word.
ambiguities: Completeness of 'all literal meanings' needs a dictionary Eko does not have; only the presence of literal + implied sets is structural.

resolution.decision: Out of the demo: Eko has no annotation or transcription input. Kept as p1.

rules.text: Separate one literal meaning set from another with a comma; separate literal sets from the implied set with a semicolon.

prefilter.notes: Structural: exactly one semicolon separating literal sets from the implied set.

ambiguities: What if a word has no implied meaning (semicolon omitted?)
A single meaning that itself contains a comma would be misparsed as two sets.

resolution.decision: Out of the demo: Eko has no annotation or transcription input. Kept as p1.
